chapter: Return to New Orleans and Sharkey
title: The Copa Club and Lester Bouchon
summary: He returned to New Orleans, worked at the Copa Club, and praises tenor player Lester Bouchon as underrated.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: So after you played in Garthport, you came back to New Orleans again?

Yeah, I came back to New Orleans, yeah. Then I worked at a club, the Copa Club. Do you remember the Copa Club on Dauphin and Devil? No. Right on that corner? Francis Jardina on that. Do you remember the Inferno? No, that was... Jimmy King? I know Jimmy King. Yeah, he owned that place. Inferno. See, I didn't come until 49 and you were with Shaw.
That's before, that's before. That was when Lester Bouchon was sick. Yeah, that's my boy. See, Lester Bouchon, he was underrated.
Well, nobody now understands that style of tenor playing except, I mean, people now don't appreciate what he was doing in a tenor.

Well, you talk to Pete Fonten, Pete Fonten thinks he's the greatest. He's a great player, and Pete Fonten likes for Zola. Yeah. Well, listen, a lot of clients, they play like Lester Bouchon, because listen, Lester can play, he can play Gut Bucket.
He can play some nice bass sax, too.
He plays bass sax and good tenor.
He plays just like Eddie Miller.
Yeah, but he's older than Eddie.

I think he's, I think, I'm, I'm, I'm, I'm not sure if he, because they used to go to school together. Oh, really? Oh, yeah, they live in the same neighborhood. Oh, that's why they almost play well, I like. Yeah. See?
I never heard Lester Nelson, but they tell me he was a good saxophone club. That's a guy that I never heard a record.
Come on, have a little few drinks, you gotta take a sip. A sip. A sip before we go.
